title: Data-Driven Environmental Analysis
description: Data-driven environmental analysis for a residential development — climate, comfort and daylight steering the massing from the first move.
body: A performance-driven environmental analysis informs the design of a residential development and landscape in Palermo. The study integrates climate assessment, massing placement optimization through an evolutionary algorithm driven by solar radiation and sea visibility, outdoor thermal comfort in Honeybee, wind analysis in infrared.city, and a design exploration across voxel-based geometries.
The final proposal cuts façade solar exposure by about 30% against a simple box while improving daylight and preserving sea views.

sections.title: Climate Analysis
body: The site's baseline: temperature, humidity, wind and radiation for Palermo, establishing which months the design actually has to work against.

sections.title: Massing Placement Optimization
body: To minimise average façade solar radiation through the hottest months, the study ran a simple box through an evolutionary search over orientation, position and building dimensions. Sea visibility is recovered by rotating the second building.

scenes.title: Sun Hours
scenes.caption: Annual sun hours across the site, averaging 10.8 hours — the input the placement search optimises against.

scenes.title: Solar Radiation
scenes.caption: Façade radiation on the baseline box seen from north-east and south-west, averaging 215.2 kWh/m².

scenes.title: Sea Visibility
scenes.caption: Visibility toward the sea, the competing objective that rotates the second building rather than simply turning it away from the sun.

sections.title: Outdoor Comfort
body: Outdoor comfort is assessed through the UTCI reduction gained from added trees, a comparison of ground materials, and urban wind analysis across the site.

scenes.title: UTCI Evaluation
scenes.caption: Universal Thermal Climate Index before and after tree integration, with ground material compared alongside.

scenes.title: Wind Analysis
scenes.caption: Dominant and maximum wind speed across the site, run in infrared.city.

sections.title: Design Concept
body: Two residential blocks and a public park, laid out from the placement study — the design proposition that the voxel exploration then tests and refines.

sections.title: Design Exploration
body: Varying the bounding box's plan dimensions and height generates a field of voxel-based geometries, compared on a parallel-coordinate chart against volume, gross floor area, solar radiation, daylight factor and visibility to select the proposal.

scenes.title: Voxel Field
scenes.caption: Fifteen voxel-based geometries generated from the bounding box parameters, with the selected proposal outlined.

scenes.title: Solar Radiation
scenes.caption: The chosen geometry drops façade radiation 27.4% against the simple box.

scenes.title: Daylight Factor
scenes.caption: Daylight factor lands 56% above the 2.5% target across the residential floors.
